neighbours.label: version-control subcommand right after 'git' / 'svn' / 'hg' (status, init, update, clone, checkout, add)
fire: To see what has changed since the last commit, type git status in the terminal.
Start a new repository by typing git init inside the project directory.
Every morning he runs svn update so that his working copy matches the server.
New contributors should first run git clone with the project's address.
Switch to the release branch with git checkout before you build.
After creating the file, tell Subversion about it with svn add and then commit.
With Mercurial, hg update moves your files to the chosen revision.
If the merge looks wrong, run svn status and read the flags in the first column.
quiet: To see what is running on the machine, type docker ps in the terminal.
Start a new project by typing cargo new inside your workspace directory.
Every morning he runs brew upgrade so that his laptop tools stay current.
New contributors should first run pip install with the project's requirements file.
The nurse will update the chart and record the patient's status at noon.
After creating the file, compile it with gcc and then run the tests.
Refresh the package index with sudo apt update before upgrading.
If the server looks wrong, run systemctl status and read the last lines of output.
